content.title: Frontal Retreat | A Collapsing Passage Forces the Only Refuge
content.summary: Let the subject face the threat and keep backing away from the target. The camera moves backward at a matching speed to keep the face and the incoming environment in the same frame. The danger occupies the passage section by section from the far end to the front, and the margin continues to shrink. Finally, the subject enters the only visible shelter and ends with the closure of the boundary.

quick_start.input_format: The subject retreats towards the threat + coaxial danger approach + staged space compression + unique asylum threshold + single boundary closure
quick_start.recommended_input: On the original paper shadow light bridge, a cream-colored jointed puppet walks backwards facing the camera, a black ink crack appears on the far end arch, and a white origami shrine is clearly visible nearby; two paper rails are folded inwards, and the clean path around the puppet is narrowed, but the identity and gait of the subject are continuous; the puppet only steps in once, and the white paper door folds and closes before the black ink arrives, and the camera remains closed, without claiming subsequent results.
required_anchors: Establish a subject facing the threat while moving backward toward a visible route.
Advance the environmental hazard along the same corridor axis as the retreat.
Keep one protective threshold readable behind the subject before the final crossing.
Use one terminal crossing and visible boundary separation from the hazard.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep a retreating subject facing an advancing hazard while a camera moves backward at matched speed; progressively reduce corridor clearance along the shared axis, preserve one visible protective threshold behind the subject, then complete one crossing and boundary closure.

invariants.rule: Establish a subject facing the threat while moving backward toward a visible route.
invariants.ablation_failure: Turning away removes simultaneous face-and-threat proof.

invariants.rule: Advance the environmental hazard along the same corridor axis as the retreat.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random off-axis debris becomes generic chaos.

invariants.rule: Reduce visible clearance in at least two stages without changing subject identity or route.
invariants.ablation_failure: One sudden blast provides no progressive pressure.

invariants.rule: Keep one protective threshold readable behind the subject before the final crossing.
invariants.purpose: Gives the retreat a clear actionable destination.
invariants.ablation_failure: A surprise exit appears as an unearned rescue.

invariants.rule: Use one terminal crossing and visible boundary separation from the hazard.
invariants.purpose: Resolves the corridor problem without claiming unseen survival.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cutting before the boundary leaves the payoff unproved.
